explanation: DeLeon treats Morales-Mota as foreclosing the argument, but Morales-Mota is a reasoned per curiam opinion printed in F.3d (704 F.3d 410), a published precedential Fifth Circuit decision; limb 1 fails.
Ramirez-Elias says Kelly 'has foreclosed this argument in this Circuit', but Kelly is a precedential F.3d opinion, issued precisely to publish part of an earlier unpublished memorandum; limb 1 fails.
Johnson cites Oshana with Back Doctors for what 'we have held' on binding stipulations; Oshana is a full signed Seventh Circuit opinion in F.3d, argued and published; limb 1 fails.

Stearns cites Windham alongside a Fifth Circuit case as support for the antitrust-injury requirement; Windham is a published, argued Fourth Circuit opinion in F.2d (en banc, from my knowledge); limbs 1 and 2 fail.

Cited item is a one-line per curiam dismissal without reasoned opinion, but it is the earlier appeal in the same Maddrie litigation, cited only as procedural history, not followed as precedent; limbs 2 and 3 fail.

The memorandum applies 'our five-factor test' from Bauman as the governing mandamus standard, but Bauman is a signed, published Ninth Circuit opinion in F.2d and settled circuit precedent; limb 1 fails.
Martinez follows Villagomez as part of 'this precedent' and 'our prior case law', but Villagomez is a full signed opinion published in Ill. App. 3d, not a Rule 23 order; limb 1 fails.
